writeup.headline: Compass rates Hold at 46, two points above Sell, as merger-driven growth meets weak quality and debt.
writeup.thesis: Compass scores 46, a Hold that sits just 2 points above the Sell line. Growth is the clear strength, scoring 100 on latest-quarter revenue growth of 109.0% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 67.8%, and growth that sped up by 9.6 pp from the previous quarter, which largely reflects the Anywhere merger. That is offset by a weak balance sheet (score 11, net debt at 19.06 times FCF and cash covering only 0.22 of debt) and soft quality (score 30), with an operating margin of -2.6%, an FCF margin of 1.2% and the diluted share count up 42.4% year on year. Valuation scores 26: P/S of 0.7x is low in absolute terms, but P/FCF of 54.1x is high in absolute terms, EBIT is negative, and the FCF yield is 3.1 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield; P/S is near the middle of the last 54 month-ends. Trend is middling at 43, with the price 32.5% below its 52-week high but shares 11.3 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, and news is neutral at 50.
key_risks: Heavy leverage: net debt at 19.06 times FCF and cash at 0.22 of debt leave little room if housing activity weakens.
Integration of the Anywhere merger may fall short of the raised $330 million actioned and $220 million realized 2026 synergy targets.
Thin profitability, with an operating margin of -2.6% and an FCF margin of 1.2%, plus the diluted share count up 42.4% year on year.
Securities class actions over the merger materials, alongside the Zillow suit, NAR class actions and a NY AG probe.
Weak price trend: shares 8.7% below their 50-day average and 7.8% below their 200-day average.
what_would_change: A 2-point drop in the score would move the rating to Sell, for example from a weak Q3 report on November 5, softer trend or negative news.
Delivering positive full-year 2026 free cash flow and paying down debt would lift the balance sheet and quality scores.
A move to Buy needs 19 more points, which would require sustained gains in quality, balance sheet and valuation, not growth alone.
